Japan holds a very special place in my heart, and every visit reminds me why. I often say
UiPath
was born in Romania, grew in Japan, and then scaled globally.

When we established UiPath there and appointed
Koichi Hasegawa
as CEO, we quickly learned that Japanese customers have some of the highest standards for product quality anywhere. Their feedback was direct and demanding, and it made our product better which is why we decided to bring our engineers to learn and build as close to them as possible. Over time, that closeness grew into a lasting partnership.

It was great to see that reflected on stage this year. SMBC,
Tokyo Electron
,
NTT DATA
, Murata Manufacturing,
Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank
and
NGK Corporation
shared how they think about where orchestration, automation and AI fit within their processes. Hearing their stories, I was reminded how much we have learned from them, and how much they are still pushing us forward.

I also had the honor of presenting the Japanese edition of my book, The Work That Remains. It felt natural to bring it here. Japan has always approached automation with a clear purpose: to elevate people’s potential, not to reduce headcount, which is one of the main themes I explored in the book. 

The next level of automation brings together deterministic technologies, which execute the same way every time, and probabilistic ones, which can reason but are not always exact. Combining them changes how enterprises design and run their processes, and it only works when AI, automation and people operate as one system, each contributing what it does best. Getting that right is the work in front of us.

Thank you to our customers, partners and the UiPath Japan team.

Our second
#UiPathFutureForwardHackathon
brought together 46 students in Bucharest to tackle this year’s challenge: Agents in Action. 👨💻👩💻

With guidance from 14 UiPath mentors and judges, students built working AI agents that addressed real-world challenges in just 24 hours.

🏅 1st place: AudioBolt, an AI agent that identifies where and when recordings were made using background sounds. 

🏅 2nd place: Splitpath, an AI agent that helps online stores test and improve conversion rates. 

🏅 3rd place: ASPY, an AI agent that verifies scientific references and flags unsupported claims. 

🏅 Special mention: UI Shapeshifter, an AI agent that adapts websites to users’ needs and preferences.

Congratulations to all our winners, and a huge thank you to the students, mentors, judges, and organizing team who made this edition possible!
